title: Amazon drone crashes on garage after delivering shampoo, draws FAA probe
gist: The FAA opened a probe after an Amazon Prime Air MK30 delivery drone clipped a fiber-optic cable and crashed onto a garage in Huntington Woods, Michigan on November 20, adding to a string of Amazon drone incidents under federal investigation even as Prime Air scales to ~6,000 daily flights and targets nearly 500 US cities and towns by end-2026.

insights.claim: On November 20, 2026, an Amazon Prime Air delivery drone lost a propeller after catching a fiber-optic cable in Huntington Woods, Michigan, and became pinned between a garage roof and power lines; the FAA has opened an investigation.
insights.speaker: Jeremy Hsu
insights.so_what: Incidents create regulatory risk for drone delivery scale-up.
insights.quote: UAS struck a fiber cable, a residential garage, and became entangled in power lines during takeoff.

insights.claim: The NTSB is gathering information on the Michigan Amazon drone crash but has not decided whether to open its own probe.
insights.speaker: Jeremy Hsu
insights.so_what: An NTSB investigation would raise the stakes and scrutiny on Prime Air operations.

insights.claim: Amazon's MK30 drones carry onboard sense-and-avoid technology, yet the drone in the Michigan crash failed to avoid a thin fiber-optic cable, highlighting a gap in obstacle detection.
insights.speaker: Jeremy Hsu
insights.so_what: Thin-wire detection is a technical weakness to watch for in drone delivery safety.

insights.claim: Amazon drone incidents under US government investigation include two drones hitting a construction crane in Tolleson, Arizona in October 2025, a drone downing an internet cable in Waco, Texas in November 2025, and a crash involving an apartment building in Richardson, Texas in February 2026.
insights.speaker: Jeremy Hsu
insights.so_what: A growing incident record could slow approvals or add operational constraints.

insights.claim: Amazon handled the Michigan crash with a team on site within 10 minutes, a promise to help repair the garage, and a $100 gift card to the homeowner, and said it was the first such crash from its Detroit-area operations.
insights.speaker: Jeremy Hsu
insights.so_what: Shows Amazon's incident-response playbook for managing local reputational fallout.
